questions.question: Match the effects of globalisation with their outcomes: (1) Increased foreign investment, (2) Cultural exchange and awareness, (3) Technological exchange and awareness, (4) Growth of multinational corporations; with (i) Expansion of global markets and access to technology, (ii) Loss of traditional jobs due to automation and cheaper labour elsewhere, (iii) Spread of cultural practices, ideas and values across borders, (iv) Large companies becoming dominant players in global markets. Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: As per the CBSE marking scheme, the answer is D: 1-i, 2-iii, 3-ii, 4-iv.
option_feedback: Foreign investment expands markets (i), not cultural spread.
Growth of MNCs makes large companies dominant (iv).
Cultural exchange spreads practices and ideas (iii).

questions.question: Highlight the significant three factors that have contributed to the growth of globalisation.
answer_steps: Transportation technology: containers loaded intact onto ships, trains, planes and trucks cut port handling costs and sped up exports; air transport became cheaper.

Information and communication technology: telephones, mobile phones, fax, satellite communication, computers and the internet allow instant contact and spread the production of services across countries.

Liberalisation of foreign trade and foreign investment policy: from 1991 India removed most barriers, so goods could be imported and exported easily and foreign companies could set up factories and offices (movement of goods, services and people also grew).

questions.question: What do you understand by globalisation? Explain in your own words.
answer_steps: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries.
It happens as more goods and services, investments and technology move between countries, mainly through MNCs that set up production in many countries and through rising foreign trade.
As a result, production and markets in different countries become closely linked; people also move, though less, because of restrictions.

questions.question: What was the reason for putting barriers to foreign trade and foreign investment by the Indian government? Why did it wish to remove these barriers?
answer_steps: After independence, the government put barriers to protect producers within the country from foreign competition, as industries were just coming up in the 1950s and 1960s; only essential items like machinery, fertilisers and petroleum were imported.
Around 1991, the government felt Indian producers were ready to compete with producers around the globe.
It believed competition would improve the performance and quality of Indian producers, so it removed barriers to a large extent (liberalisation).

questions.question: How has liberalisation of trade and investment policies helped the globalisation process?
answer_steps: Liberalisation removed government barriers such as taxes on imports, so goods could be imported and exported easily.
Foreign companies were allowed to set up factories and offices, increasing foreign investment by MNCs.
Businesses could freely decide what to import and export, which increased foreign trade and integrated production and markets across countries.

questions.question: What is an MNC? Why does it set up production in other countries?
answer_steps: An MNC is a company that owns or controls production in more than one nation.
It sets up production where it can get cheap labour and resources and be near markets, so its costs are low and profits high.

questions.question: How did containers help globalisation?
answer_steps: Goods are placed in containers that can be loaded intact onto ships, railways, planes and trucks.
This reduced port handling costs and increased the speed with which exports reach markets.

questions.question: What is a trade barrier? Why do governments use it?
answer_steps: A trade barrier is a restriction on foreign trade, such as a tax on imports.
Governments use it to regulate foreign trade, deciding what kinds of goods and how much of each come into the country.

questions.question: Explain how MNCs, foreign investment and foreign trade together lead to globalisation.
answer_steps: MNCs look for locations around the world where production is cheap, so their foreign investment in these countries has been rising.
At the same time, foreign trade between countries has been rising rapidly, and a large part of it is controlled by MNCs.
Greater foreign investment and trade have integrated production and markets across countries; this rapid integration is globalisation.

questions.question: How has information and communication technology helped globalisation?
answer_steps: Telecommunication facilities like telephones, mobile phones and fax, aided by satellites, let people contact each other and access information instantly, even from remote areas.
Computers and the internet let people share information and send e-mail across the world at negligible cost.
IT spreads the production of services across countries, for example a London magazine designed and printed in Delhi and paid for by internet banking.

questions.question: Compare India's trade policy before and after 1991.
answer_steps: Before 1991: the government put barriers on foreign trade and investment to protect new domestic industries; only essential imports like machinery, fertilisers and petroleum were allowed.
After 1991: the government decided Indian producers should compete globally, and removed barriers to a large extent.
Goods could now be imported and exported easily, foreign companies could set up factories and offices, and businesses could decide freely what to trade.

questions.question: What is globalisation? Explain the different ways in which countries are connected through it.
answer_steps: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries.
Goods and services move between countries through rising foreign trade, a large part of which is controlled by MNCs.
Investment moves between countries as MNCs set up factories and offices abroad; this foreign investment has been rising.
Technology moves across countries, and IT spreads the production of services, linking producers and markets worldwide.
People also move in search of better income, jobs or education, but this movement has not increased much because of restrictions.

questions.question: Explain the factors that have enabled globalisation.
answer_steps: Transportation technology: containers loaded intact onto ships, trains, planes and trucks reduced port handling costs and sped up exports; air transport became cheaper.

Information and communication technology: telephones, mobile phones, fax and satellite communication allow instant contact; computers and the internet let information and services move across the world at negligible cost.
IT helps spread the production of services, such as designing and printing a London magazine in Delhi with payment by internet banking.
Liberalisation of foreign trade and investment: after independence India used trade barriers to protect new industries, but from 1991 it removed most barriers so producers would compete globally.
With liberalisation, goods could be imported and exported easily and foreign companies could set up factories and offices, increasing foreign trade and investment.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor that has stimulated the globalisation process. For instance, the past fifty years have seen several improvements in transportation technology. This has made much faster delivery of goods across long distances possible at lower costs."* (NCERT)

(i) Name one improvement in transportation technology that helped globalisation. (1)

(ii) How did it help? (1)

(iii) Give two examples of information and communication technology that helped globalisation. (2)
answer_steps: (i) The use of containers (or cheaper air transport).
(ii) Containers reduced port handling costs and increased the speed of exports.
(iii) Any two: telephones and mobile phones; fax; satellite communication; computers; the internet and e-mail; internet banking.

questions.question:
Read the source and answer the questions.

*"Starting around 1991, some far-reaching changes in policy were made in India. The government decided that the time had come for Indian producers to compete with producers around the globe. It felt that competition would improve the performance of producers within the country since they would have to improve their quality."* (NCERT)

(i) What did the government decide around 1991? (1)

(ii) Why did it expect competition to help? (1)

(iii) What is liberalisation? How did it help globalisation? (2)
answer_steps: (i) That Indian producers should compete with producers around the globe, so trade and investment barriers were removed.
(ii) Competition would force producers to improve their quality and performance.

(iii) Liberalisation is removing government barriers on trade and investment; it let goods be imported and exported easily and foreign companies set up in India, increasing integration with other countries.
